sourceEvidence.title: Thailand: The Chakkri Dynasty
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: Body: Rama I founded dynasty in 1782 and moved court to Bangkok; nineteenth-century royal diplomacy and monarchy. No automatic dynastic succession rule and suzerainty distinct from modern boundaries.

sourceEvidence.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sourceEvidence.title: Thailand: 1932 Coup
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: Body: absolute monarchy ended 24 June 1932; provisional constitution three days later; permanent constitution before year end; National Assembly and cabinet with practical promoter/Army power; 1933 suspension/restoration and 1935 regency.

sourceEvidence.title: The National Assembly of Thailand: parliamentary guide
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: PDF historical pages 4–5: 24 June 1932 transition, temporary act 27 June, nominated first assembly 28 June. Formal constitutional change does not by itself establish unrestricted democracy.

sourceEvidence.institution: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand, edited by Dr Dhiravat na Pombejra
sourceEvidence.title: Historical chronology: Ayutthaya to Bangkok (Rattanakosin)
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: PDF page 4 explicitly identifies accession of Rama I in 1782 as the beginning of Chakri Dynasty and Bangkok (Rattanakosin) era; establishes the historical name link, not later automatic government continuity.

reviews.semanticAndRoleCaveat: Historical alias mapping is established by the existing LOC Thailand Chakkri history and Thai MFA chronology source usage, explicitly describing the Siam/Bangkok dynastic framework. Original P36 alleges Bangkok from1767 (year), conflicting with the accepted registry source reporting Rama I moved court to Bangkok1782. Accept only1800–1932 framework interiors, independently later than1782; do not accept1767 as inception, repair it to1782, or infer modern Thai sovereignty.

reviews.subject: Q252

value.text: Indonesia names new capital Nusantara, replacing sinking Jakarta

existence.note: Editorial bounds delimit a partial source-supported dossier, not a complete state lifetime or universal territorial control.

sourceEvidence.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sourceEvidence.title: Indonesia: The Constitution
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: Body paragraphs 1–10: provisional constitution 18 August 1945; sovereignty transfer/federal constitution 27 December 1949; unitary cabinet constitution ratified August 1950; martial law 14 March 1957; dissolution of Constituent Assembly and return to 1945 constitution 5 July 1959. Later New Order institutions omitted.

sourceEvidence.title: Address on the 64th anniversary of the proclamation, 14 August 2009
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: Historical body distinguishes 17 August proclamation, next-day constitution and 5 July 1959 return to the 1945 constitution; presidential Guided Democracy through 1966. Broad shorthand for all 1945–1959 parliamentary institutions not adopted.

sourceEvidence.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sourceEvidence.title: FRUS 1958–1960, XVII, Document 224, 10 September 1959
sourceEvidence.usage: Body read: Opening body explicitly dates first Guided Democracy cabinet under Sukarno premiership to 10 July 1959; Army expanding practical role and party exclusions. Later regime continuity corroborated by historical presidential address, not extrapolated from this single memo alone.

reviews.semanticAndRoleCaveat: The accepted registry explicitly identifies the Republic of Indonesia Guided Democracy framework from1959-07-10. Preferred dated Jakarta statement begins1950-08-17; previous historical capitals end by that date. Deprecated Nusantara with unknown start is excluded. Mapping capital only does not import pre1959 regime or modern territorial control.
